A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExoFormer research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original 450M-model training experiments, downstream benchmark scores, normalization and granularity comparisons, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds 1B-model training curves, anchor interventions, anchor-depth experiments, normalization tests, and gradient diagnostics.

M1.justification: The core normalized Q/K/V/G mixing and dynamic coefficient generator remain unchanged. v4 adds limited architectural variants using H1 or H2 anchor sources instead of H0 (Section 4.6), and additional post-mixing QKV or QKVG normalization (Appendix E).

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu and the same six downstream benchmarks: ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, and WinoGrande. Larger models, additional training tokens, and architectural interventions do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set matches between v1 Table 3 and v4 Table 1. However, the gate-profile comparison removes Dynamic ExoFormer: it appears in v1 Figure 5 but not v4 Figure 8. Newly discussed methods such as YOCO and SkipV1Former are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds approximately 1B-parameter, 32-layer, width-1536 experiments trained for 20B tokens with lower learning rates, extending v1's 450M/10B setting (Figure 2 and Table 8). New protocols include inference-time coefficient-zeroing controls and gradient-spike measurement using a 1,000-step rolling window. The original 450M five-shot benchmark protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds anchor-removal and current-projection-removal interventions, H0/H1/H2 anchor-depth tests, additional post-mixing normalization ablations, and quantitative gradient-stability analysis (Sections 4.5-4.6; Appendices C, E, F). These substantially extend v1's normalization, granularity, gating, and representation analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4's rolling-standard-deviation threshold defines an optimization diagnostic; it does not add uncertainty reporting for experimental performance.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark entries change: E-ExoFormer's ARC-C score goes from 34.73 to 32.42, and H-ExoFormer's WinoGrande score from 54.06 to 52.72, reconciling the retained averages. Table 2 changes substantially: Dynamic ExoFormer's PCA features change from 752.1 to 885.0, token similarity from 0.8622 to 0.6606, and attention sink from 0.0073 to 0.0453. v4 also adds larger-model curves and intervention results, including dynamic H1-anchor perplexity of 14.02.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix D adds parameter and FLOP overhead derivations absent from v1, including separate anchor, static-mixing, and dynamic-module contributions and relative overhead formulas (Equations 15-26). This is a substantial new analytical component. Neither version provides a formal proof of the Offloading Hypothesis.

C1.justification: v4 removes the headline claims that intact ExoFormer exhibits representation collapse and halves attention sinks relative to Gated Attention. It reframes the advertised accuracy/data-efficiency comparison from 2.13 points and 1.84 times fewer tokens against the base Transformer to approximately 1.5 points and 1.5 times against Gated Attention, and adds the benefit of deeper anchor sources.

C2.justification: v4 replaces the interpretation of intact-model collapse as useful signal purification with an argument based on collapse after anchor removal. It adds explanations for anchor-depth effects, diminishing normalization returns, and practical runtime overhead. v1's explicit limitations concerning long contexts, coefficient initialization, and the missing theoretical explanation are omitted; uncertainty about substantially larger models remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds the 1B configuration and learning rates in Table 8, procedures for the new interventions, and a model-access hyperlink alongside the retained code link. Most 450M hyperparameters and hardware details remain. v1's explicit terminal learning rate of 10% of the peak is no longer stated.

R1.justification: v4 adds positioning against SkipV1Former, YOCO, and CRnet, and cites OLMo 2 for gradient diagnostics. It removes the Hoffmann and Hagele references accompanying earlier scaling and scheduling discussion. The central relationship to ResFormer and MUDDFormer remains; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v4 moves the comprehensive benchmark results and granularity discussion from appendices into the main text, substantially rewrites the offloading narrative, removes the separate Limitations section, and reorganizes the appendices. The abstract, conclusion, related-work discussion, and title are also revised.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. Architecture and training displays are separated, larger-model and ablation displays are added, and representation and gating plots are redrawn. The comprehensive benchmark table moves into the main text, Table 2 is transposed, and two panels from v1's six-panel representation figure are dropped.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens v1's largely correlational mechanistic case with controlled anchor interventions, checks the validation-loss advantage at 1B scale, and examines normalization, gradient stability, and practical runtime costs. Benchmark-cell revisions also restore arithmetic consistency. Strong causal interpretations and the removal of several explicit limitations remain weaknesses, but the new mechanistic tests and cost evidence provide a substantial overall quality gain.
